slices.basis: Singular identities derived by calendar-spine from the independently source-backed calendar publication, not from held propers. This closes fixed-calendar identity enumeration only: neither per-formulary slots, territorial additions, movable celebrations nor text coverage.

Introit antiphon+psalm, gradual, tract and paired Alleluia remain compound functional appointments; their verses/repetitions are not multiplied. slices.basis: Independent enumeration from the exact facsimile SHA-256 648fdb8fe830ed65a08aa4a95de6f94424c533ddf2398c8fc26b18735fd3518a, artifact pp. 144–210 / printed pp. 63–129: from the Dominica I in Quadragesima heading (after marginal 427 on the same page) through marginal 825 on p. 210; Hebdomada sancta begins p. 211 at marginal 826. 36 formularies (35 days; the Lent Ember Saturday long and short forms are printed separately), all 398 numbered proper units 428–825 with their semantic roles, 36 unnumbered Preface appointments, two conditional ordination-oration referrals, Credo and other explicit Ordinary directions and use referrals. Roles were checked mechanically against the raw extraction (the OCR role-heading sequence of every formulary is a subsequence of the enumerated sequence; 350 of 398 numbers located with matching pages) and every unlocated number or missed heading was confirmed on page images. Completeness is bounded to these local printed proper units and explicit appointments, not the whole Ordinary, every rubrical combination, or text wording. No held propers were used.

slices.basis: All 60 explicit Mass formularies from Easter through the last Sunday after Pentecost, including both long/short forms of Pentecost and September Ember Saturday, and all 639 numbered proper text appointments (1140–1778). Numbered compound chants remain compound slots; no inferred civil-date occurrence universe.

boundaries.basis: The calendar identifies celebrations and commemorations; it does not enumerate every appointed text, alternative, proper preface or Common reference. No text-slot denominator is inferred from these identities.
